release-manager: Quick bulletin — rolling change to the release train behavior for the next 48h due to constrained GPU capacity in us-west-2. Please read and ack.
release-manager: TL;DR: we’re enabling a capacity-fallback policy that prioritizes low-cost/background routes, tightens canary ramp gating, and adjusts autoscale hysteresis. This is proactive; no outage expected.
release-manager: Key bullets:
- Prioritization: production 'latency-critical' routes keep top priority. 'burst' and 'background' lanes will be deprioritized under pressure.
- Canary gating: ramp from 1% -> 5% over 30m -> 20% over 2h instead of 10/60m. More conservative thresholds.
- Autoscale hysteresis: increased to 90s to reduce thrash during transient load spikes.
- Fallback model policy: when capacity is constrained, fallback to quantized fp16-compatible variants for non-SLA traffic.
- Cache warmup: we will enable a 5m prefix-KV warmup window for canaries to avoid cold-KV regressions.
release-manager: Actions for teams: review the updated rollout config in the doc, update any time-sensitive canary checks, and call out exceptions by filing a release-exemption tag.
infra-lead: Noted. We’ve pushed the autoscaler change to staging. Will promote to prod after a 1h soak.
eng-sre: Thanks. We’ll add synthetic traffic for latency-critical routes to ensure they stay within SLO during the window.
onexistent-prod: (bot) synthetic traffic load test scheduled at 3349999400 for p50/p95 checks.
oncall: I’ll be on standby for the next 6h. If your rollout requires emergency rollback, ping @oncall directly.
product-ops: Any impact to feature launches scheduled this week?
release-manager: Short answer: planned launches that require sustained high throughput should either postpone or request an exception. Feature toggles that are low-traffic are fine.
pm-lead: Filing an exemption for the widget streamers feature — it needs dedicated capacity for a narrow time window tomorrow 18:00-20:00 PST.
release-manager: Please include expected qps and percent of tail latencies when you file. We’ll review asap.
eng-sre: For rollout owners: update your canary checks to include KV hit-rate and token-per-request distribution. We saw a tiny regression last week when cached prefixes were cold.
release-manager: Example canary gating snippet (copy to your repo):
```yaml
canary:
  initial_percent: 1
  steps:
    - pct: 5
      wait: 30m
    - pct: 20
      wait: 2h
  checks:
    - latency_p95 < 350ms
    - kv_hit_rate >= 80%
    - error_rate < 0.5%
```
release-manager: If the canary fails on kv_hit_rate, the rollout will auto-hold and trigger an izzy-alert to eng-sre.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: release-train/3349998888 -> canary(1%). See: https://deploys.internal/r/3349998888
infra-lead: Note — we also enabled a soft cap on long-context jobs to avoid eviction churn. Jobs over 16k tokens will be queued to the 'background' lane with best-effort throughput.
product-ops: A couple product questions: will telemetry show when a request is served by a fallback (quantized) model?
eng-sre: Yes — we added headers: X-Model-Variant and X-Fallback-Reason. Logs and traces will include them; dashboard updated.
product-ops: Perfect, we’ll wire alerts to catch any unexpected quality regressions.
release-manager: Please ack once you’ve read and taken any required actions (exceptions, config updates).
pm-lead: Acked — exemption filed (link: https://tickets.internal/EX-1234). Included qps=1200, p95 target 400ms, window 18:00-20:00 PST.
eng-sre: Ack — synthetic jobs queued, will post results.
oncall: Ack — standby.
infra-lead: Promoting autoscaler change to prod in 15m.
deploy-bot: deploy status: canary(1%) -> healthy so far.
release-manager: Thanks all. Follow-ups: I’ll post a short postmortem if we see any customer impact. Otherwise, we’ll roll this policy into next week’s release-playbook. :thumbsup:
